hero.subtitle: A collision on Whittier Boulevard or Lambert Road can upend your week in seconds. We help Whittier drivers and passengers with car accident claims at no upfront cost.

about.title: Whittier Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Whittier sits where the San Gabriel Valley meets the Gateway Cities, and its streets carry a steady mix of commuters, students, and neighborhood traffic. In 2025, Los Angeles County public records logged 443 injury collisions inside the city, with 599 people hurt and 7 lives lost. Whittier Boulevard, Lambert Road, Beverly Boulevard, and Painter Avenue account for the largest share of those reports, and Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. show the highest counts. Behind each number is a person trying to figure out what comes next. If that is you, we can help. We listen to what happened and work directly on your claim. We handle car accident cases on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. California gives you two years to file in most cases, but far less if a city or county vehicle was involved. Getting guidance early keeps your options open while you focus on getting better.
about.commonInjuriesTitle: Injuries We Commonly See After Whittier Car Crashes
commonInjuries: Herniated discs and lower back injuries
Knee and shoulder damage from impact
Cuts and bruising from airbags or glass
about.ctaText: Tell us what happened. Get your free case review.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't Close the Door
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so you can still pursue a claim even if you were partly responsible; your share of blame simply reduces the recovery rather than erasing it. We can push back when an insurer tries to inflate your percentage.

items.title: Deadlines That Are Easy to Miss
items.desc: Most Whittier car accident claims must be filed within two years, but a crash involving a city bus, county truck, or other government vehicle may require a claim in as little as six months. We track those clocks from the start.

items.title: Evidence and Statements Handled Carefully
items.desc: Photos, dashcam footage, and witness names fade fast, and the other driver's insurer will likely ask for a recorded statement you are not required to give. We handle those communications on your behalf and work to preserve evidence before it disappears.

items.question: I was hit on Whittier Boulevard during Friday evening traffic. What should I do first?
items.answer: Get medical attention even if you feel mostly fine, since neck and back symptoms often show up a day or two later. Save the police report number, photos of both vehicles, and the names of anyone who stopped to help. Then reach out to us; our team can start preserving evidence before it disappears.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company keeps calling for a recorded statement. Do I have to give one?
items.answer: No. You are not obligated to give a recorded statement to another party's insurer, and adjusters are trained to ask questions in ways that can shrink your claim. A polite refusal is fine. Once you contact us, we can handle those conversations on your behalf.

items.question: How much does it cost to get help with my car accident claim?
items.answer: Nothing upfront. We handle car accident cases on contingency, which means we are paid only if there is a recovery, and you will discuss those terms directly with us before agreeing to anything.
